Do not say ‘I work harder’ or ‘I’m passionate’ — be specific. Line 3: Offer one concrete next step with zero pressure. Example: a no-obligation updated market assessment. Do not pitch a listing mandate in this message. Line 4: Close warmly with the agent’s name. No formal sign-off for WhatsApp. - If a reason for expiry was provided, reference it subtly in line 1 or 2. - If no reason was provided, keep the tone general but still empathetic. - Match channel tone: WhatsApp: conversational, warm, short sentences, no formal sign-off Email: structured, slightly more formal, include a subject line above the body Format as: SUBJECT: [subject line] followed by a blank line, then the body Handwritten note: very short, personal, 3 sentences maximum, warm close - Never use the phrase ‘I understand how frustrating that must be’ - Never mention price reductions in this first message - The goal is to open a conversation, not to close a deal 4–6 sentence length | Expired listing sellers are cautious and have already been let down once. A longer message feels like another sales pitch. A shorter message feels dismissive. 4–6 sentences is the sweet spot — enough to show you understand their situation, short enough to not overwhelm. Email subject line format | When the channel is email, the agent needs a subject line too. By instructing the AI to prepend ‘SUBJECT: [line]’, the agent gets a complete email in one output. No second step required. No negative competitor mentions | Criticising the previous agent backfires. It makes the new agent sound desperate and unprofessional. The prompt explicitly bans this. Instead, the message differentiates through what the agent offers, not what the competitor failed to do. No mandate pitch | The biggest mistake agents make in expired listing outreach is asking for the listing too early. The prompt restricts the AI to offering a market assessment — a low-stakes next step that gets a foot in the door without pressure. WhatsApp deep-link | The output is immediately actionable. The agent does not need to open WhatsApp, find the contact, and paste the message manually. One tap pre-fills the message body. This is the ‘fast beats free’ principle applied to the result page. You are a senior frontend developer specialising in mobile-first web applications. Build a single-page web application called the Instant Lead Response Generator for real estate agents. === PRODUCT BRIEF === Purpose: A real estate agent receives a new inbound lead notification on their phone. They open this tool, fill in 4 fields in under 30 seconds, tap Generate, and get a personalised first-contact message ready to send immediately. Speed is the entire product. Every design decision serves speed. Target user: South African real estate agent, on their phone, in the field. This is the most mobile-critical tool in the suite. Design for 390px first. === DESIGN SPECIFICATION === Use identical design system as Tools 1 and 2 with these mobile-specific additions: Mobile-first rules (non-negotiable): - All input fields: minimum height 52px (larger than Tools 1 & 2 for field use) - Font size on inputs: 16px minimum (prevents iOS auto-zoom on focus) - Submit button: full width, 56px height - No horizontal scroll at any viewport width from 320px up - Tested on: iPhone SE (375px), iPhone 14 (390px), Samsung Galaxy (360px) Header copy: Headline: ‘Respond before they call someone else.’ Subheadline: ‘A personalised first-contact message. Sent in under 15 seconds.’ Speed indicator (unique to this tool): Below the subheadline, add a small stat badge: Background: #FEF9C3, border: 1px solid #FDE68A, border-radius: 20px Padding: 4px 12px, display inline-block Text (DM Sans 12px 500, color #92400E): ‘Responding within 5 min = 9x higher conversion’ No icon, no tooltip — just the text === INPUT FORM === STRICT MAXIMUM: 4 fields only. No exceptions. No optional fields on this tool. Field 1: Lead’s First Name Label: ‘Lead’s first name’ Type: Text input Placeholder: ‘e.g. Mpho’ autocomplete: given-name autofocus on page load (desktop only — not mobile to avoid keyboard popup) Field 2: Property They Enquired About Label: ‘What property did they enquire about?’ Type: Text input Placeholder: ‘e.g. 3-bed in Fourways / 14 Acacia Street’ Helper text (13px #6B7280): ‘Area and type is fine if no specific property’ Field 3: Lead Source Label: ‘Where did this lead come from?’ Type: Select dropdown (native select — no custom dropdown) Options: - Property24 - Private Property - Facebook Ad - Instagram - Referral from a client - Walk-in / call-in - Other Placeholder: ‘Select lead source…’ Field 4: Your First Name Label: ‘Your first name’ Type: Text input Placeholder: ‘e.g. Zanele’ Submit Button: Text: ‘Generate My Response’ Full width, 56px height, background #111111, text white, 8px radius Loading: animated dots ‘···’ cycling — no spinner (cleaner on mobile) === OUTPUT SECTION === Same output pattern as Tools 1 and 2 with these additions: Label: ‘Your response is ready — send it now’ (Urgency language is intentional here — speed is the entire product) Output box: same JetBrains Mono, green background Action buttons (3, stacked vertically on mobile for large tap targets): Button 1: ‘Copy Response’ — same behaviour as Tools 1 & 2 Button 2: ‘Send via WhatsApp’ — wa.me deep link (always visible, not just for WhatsApp leads) wa.me/?text={encodeURIComponent(outputText)} Style: border 1px solid #25D366, color #25D366 Button 3: ‘Generate Again’ — same behaviour as Tools 1 & 2 On mobile (max-width 520px): buttons stack vertically, full width, 48px each On desktop: buttons display in a row === CTA SECTION === Headline: ‘That response took 7 seconds.’ Body: ‘Most agents reply to leads 4 hours later and wonder why they lose them. Book a free Funnel Audit — I’'‘ll walk you through exactly what your lead journey looks like and where it’'‘s costing you deals.’ Button: ‘Book My Free Audit →’ Link: [INSERT_CALENDLY_URL] === BACKEND / API CALL === Same API structure as Tools 1 and 2. Dynamic user message construction: ‘Lead’s name: {leadName} Property they enquired about: {propertyDescription} Lead source: {leadSource} My name: {agentName} Generate my first-contact response now.’ === SYSTEM PROMPT === You are a high-performance real estate sales coach and conversion copywriter. Your job is to write a first-contact message from a real estate agent to a new inbound lead. The message must feel personal, warm, and immediate. STRICT OUTPUT RULES: - Output ONLY the final message. No preamble, no label, no explanation. - Length: 3 to 4 sentences maximum. This is a first message, not a pitch. - The message must: 1. Open by acknowledging the specific property or area they enquired about. Make it feel like the agent actually read their enquiry. 2. Establish the agent as a helpful resource, not a salesperson. 3. Ask ONE qualifying question to start a conversation. Good: ‘Are you looking to move in the next few months, or just exploring?’ Bad: ‘What’s your budget?’ (too forward for a first message) 4. Close naturally with the agent’s name. No formal sign-off. - Tone must always be warm, fast, and conversational. This is a WhatsApp-style message even if the channel is not specified. Short sentences. Natural rhythm. Zero corporate language. - Do NOT say ‘Thank you for your enquiry’ — sounds automated. - Do NOT say ‘I saw your enquiry on Property24’ — sounds like a CRM alert. Instead, reference the property naturally: ‘The listing in Fourways…’ - Source-specific tone adjustments: Property24 / Private Property: Fast and direct. Lead was browsing actively. Facebook / Instagram Ad: Re-establish context in line 1. They may have forgotten they enquired. Referral: Open with a warm reference to the mutual connection. ‘Zanele mentioned you were looking — great to connect.’ Walk-in / call-in: They already showed high intent. Message can be more direct about next steps. - The single most important outcome: get a reply. Every sentence should invite a response, not deliver information. 3–4 sentence maximum | A first contact message that is too long signals that the agent is desperate or inexperienced. Short messages have higher open and reply rates on WhatsApp. The constraint forces the AI to prioritise what matters most. One qualifying question | Asking multiple questions in a first message is overwhelming. One good question opens a dialogue. The prompt specifies what makes a good qualifying question versus a bad one because without this, the AI defaults to asking about budget — which kills the conversation. No ‘thank you for your enquiry’ | This phrase is the loudest signal that the response came from a CRM auto-reply. It destroys the illusion that a real human responded within seconds. The prompt bans it explicitly. Source-specific tone logic | A Facebook ad lead and a referral lead are in completely different psychological states. A Facebook lead may not even remember enquiring. A referral lead already has warm context. The same message sent to both will underperform for one of them. The prompt handles this inside the system instructions rather than requiring extra form fields. WhatsApp deep-link always visible | Unlike Tool 2 where the WhatsApp button is conditional on channel selection, this tool shows the WhatsApp button regardless — because almost all South African agent-to-lead communication happens on WhatsApp regardless of how the lead came in. Add an email capture gate to the tool. The gate appears AFTER the agent clicks Generate and BEFORE the result is shown. === BEHAVIOUR === 1. Agent fills in form and clicks Generate. 2. The API call fires immediately in the background (do not wait for email submission). 3. While the API call is in progress, show the email gate overlay on top of the form. 4. The agent enters their email and clicks the gate’s submit button. 5. When BOTH conditions are met (API call complete AND email submitted), hide the gate and show the result. 6. If the API call finishes before the email is entered, hold the result and show it immediately when the email is submitted. 7. If the email is submitted before the API call finishes, show a brief animated loading state on the gate button until the result is ready. === DESIGN === The gate is NOT a blocking modal. It replaces the form area inline. No overlay, no dimming, no popup. Container: same white card as the form, same padding Headline (DM Serif Display 24px): ‘Where should we send insights like this?’ Subtext (DM Sans 14px #6B7280): ‘Drop your email and get your result instantly. We send weekly conversion tips for agents. Unsubscribe any time.’ Input: email type, placeholder ‘your@email.com’, full width, 48px height Button: ‘Get My Result →’, full width, #111111 background, 48px height Fine print (12px #9CA3AF, centred below button): ‘No spam. Just one email a week. Unsubscribe any time.’ === INTEGRATION === On email submission, POST to your email provider’s API or form endpoint. Suggested: ConvertKit form embed OR a simple fetch to a serverless function that adds the email to your list and tags it with the tool name. Tag the subscriber: ‘tool-1-objection’ / ‘tool-2-expired’ / ‘tool-3-new-lead’ This lets you segment follow-up emails by which tool they used. If the email POST fails, still show the result — never block the user experience for a failed email capture. Log the error silently. === SKIP OPTION === Add a small text link below the fine print: ‘Skip for now’ Style: 11px, #9CA3AF, no underline, cursor pointer On click: hide the gate and show the result immediately No guilt-tripping copy. No ‘No thanks, I don’t want better results.’ Just ‘Skip for now’. Why This Gate Works The agent has already invested 30 seconds filling in the form and clicking Generate. At this point, their psychological commitment is high. Asking for an email here converts at 3–5x the rate of asking for it upfront. The API call fires in parallel so the result is ready almost instantly after email submission — maintaining the 15-second promise. Convert the existing single-file HTML prototype into a production Next.js application. === REQUIREMENTS === Framework: Next.js 14 with App Router Hosting target: Vercel (free tier sufficient) API key security: Move the Anthropic API key to a server-side Route Handler. The key must NEVER appear in client-side code or be visible in browser devtools. === FILE STRUCTURE === app/ layout.js — root layout with Google Fonts import page.js — tool homepage (the form) globals.css — shared styles api/ generate/ route.js — POST handler that calls Anthropic API server-side .env.local — ANTHROPIC_API_KEY=sk-ant-… === API ROUTE HANDLER (route.js) === Accept POST with JSON body: { systemPrompt, userMessage } Validate that both fields are present and non-empty strings. Reject requests where systemPrompt does not match one of the 3 approved templates. (This prevents prompt injection from malicious users.) Call Anthropic API server-side using the ANTHROPIC_API_KEY environment variable. Return the generated text as JSON: { result: string } Handle errors: return { error: string } with appropriate HTTP status code. === RATE LIMITING === Add basic rate limiting to the API route: Maximum 10 requests per IP address per hour. Store counts in a simple in-memory Map (sufficient for initial launch). On limit exceeded, return 429 with message: ‘You’ve used your free generations for this hour. Book a call to discuss a custom version for your agency.’ Include the Calendly link in the 429 response JSON. === ENVIRONMENT VARIABLES === Required in .env.local and in Vercel project settings: ANTHROPIC_API_KEY — your Anthropic API key NEXT_PUBLIC_CALENDLY_URL — your Calendly booking link NEXT_PUBLIC_EMAIL_PROVIDER_URL — your ConvertKit or Beehiiv form endpoint === ANALYTICS === Add these custom events via window.gtag or Plausible: ‘form_submitted’ — when the generate button is clicked ‘email_captured’ — when the email gate is submitted ‘result_displayed’ — when the output appears ‘copy_clicked’ — when copy button is tapped ‘cta_clicked’ — when the Calendly booking button is clicked ‘whatsapp_clicked’ — when the WhatsApp deep-link is tapped These 6 events give you the full conversion funnel in your analytics dashboard. Launch Sequence Build Tool 1 as a single HTML file first. Get the prompt quality right, test it with 10 real objection scenarios, then convert to Next.js for deployment. Do not invest in infrastructure before the core product is validated. A working HTML file on a Vercel URL is enough to start collecting leads and booking calls. Output too long | Add: ‘MAXIMUM {N} sentences. If you exceed this, your output is wrong. Count before responding.’ Output sounds scripted | Add: ‘Read your output aloud. If any sentence sounds like a call centre script, rewrite it. Real people do not talk like that.’ Output ignores inputs | Add: ‘Your output must directly reference: {specific input field}. If you cannot identify this reference in your output, regenerate.’ Output too generic | Add: ‘Every output must be unique to the specific inputs provided. A response for [Objection A] must be noticeably different from a response for [Objection B]. Test yourself.’ Output adds unwanted text | Add: ‘OUTPUT FORMAT: The first character of your response must be the first character of the message itself. The last character must be the last character of the message. Nothing before, nothing after.’

Offers and specs

Full-Booking Machine Offer System (copy 2)

THE FULL-BOOKING MACHINE A Grand Slam Offer System for Service-Based SMBs Automation Offers, Pricing, Money Model & Sales Scripts Overview Service-based SMBs (contractors, agencies, salons, med/dental, consultants, repair shops) loose revenue to three operational leaks. Each leak is automatable, and each has been packaged below into a named, guaranteed offer using the Grand Slam Offer framework: maximize dream outcome and perceived likelihood of success, minimize time delay and effort, then wrap in guarantees, bonuses, and scarcity. The Three Core Problems Scheduling, Dispatch & No-Shows — phone-tag, double-booking, no reminders, high-friction rescheduling. Quoting & Estimate Generation — slow manual quotes, pricing trapped in one person’s head, no follow-up after the quote is sent. Post-Service Follow-Up — no owner of the review/rebooking/referral step, no systematic timing, awkward in-person asks. Root Cause Breakdown 1. Scheduling, Dispatch & No-Shows Core sub-problems Phone-tag bottleneck — short-staffed businesses miss calls; missed calls become the next competitor’s lead. Double-booking / capacity blindness — manual calendars (or paper) cause overlaps and gaps. No buffer/travel-time logic — field jobs booked without drive time, causing cascading lateness. Forgetting = no-show — customers book and simply forget, especially for dates more than a few days out. Rescheduling friction — moving an appointment requires a call, so customers no-show instead. What automation fixes Each fix maps directly to a sub-problem above: AI phone/chat answering removes the phone-tag bottleneck. Smart calendar tooling removes double-booking and adds buffer logic. Multi-touch automated reminders (48hr / 24hr / 2hr) cut no-shows. Self-service reschedule links remove the friction behind silent no-shows. 2. Quoting & Estimate Generation Core sub-problems Estimation requires manual site visits/measurement, adding days of delay. Pricing logic lives in the owner’s head — a single point of failure for quoting. Quote formatting/assembly is a manual 20-30 minute task that gets deprioritized. No urgency after the quote is sent — warm leads go cold waiting. Inconsistent pricing across similar jobs erodes trust and margin. What automation fixes Each fix maps directly to a sub-problem above: Photo-based AI estimating or structured intake forms remove the need for an in-person visit. Templated pricing rules capture the owner’s knowledge into a repeatable system. Auto-generated, branded quote documents remove assembly time. Automated follow-up sequences keep quoted leads warm without manual chasing. 3. Post-Service Follow-Up (Reviews, Rebooking, Referrals) Core sub-problems Nobody owns the follow-up step once a job is marked done. Timing is manual and inconsistent — asks happen sporadically, not systematically. No visibility into rebooking windows for recurring-service customers. Asking for referrals in person feels awkward, so it rarely happens. Review requests aren’t filtered, risking public complaints from unhappy customers. What automation fixes Each fix maps directly to a sub-problem above: Job-completion triggers auto-fire a follow-up sequence with zero reliance on staff memory. Timed drip campaigns solve the rebooking blind spot for recurring services. Automated, well-timed referral asks remove the awkward in-person moment. Pre-filtered review requests protect the public rating while still capturing feedback. The Three Grand Slam Offers Offer 1 — “The Never-Miss System” (Scheduling / No-Shows) Dream Outcome Fill every open slot on the calendar and never lose a job to a missed call or a no-show again. Core Promise “We’ll recover $[X] in lost bookings in your first 14 days — using your own missed-call log as the baseline — or we run it free until we do, and you keep everything we built.” The Stack AI phone/chat answering that books jobs 24/7, even after hours Smart calendar with auto-buffer/travel-time logic 3-touch automated reminder sequence (48hr / 24hr / 2hr) One-click self-serve reschedule Missed-call text-back so no lead calls a competitor Guarantee Performance-based, tied to a measurable number recovered within 14 days — not a vague activity promise. Bonus A done-for-you missed-call recovery in week one — a fast, visible win using real texted-back leads before asking for any long-term commitment. Offer 2 — “Quote-to-Close in 24 Hours” (Quoting) Dream Outcome Turn every inquiry into a professional quote same-day, without lifting a finger — and win more jobs by being first to respond. Core Promise “Every inquiry gets a professional quote in under an hour, automatically — and if your close rate doesn’t go up within 30 days, we don’t just refund you, we pay you $[X] for wasting your time.” The Stack Structured intake form / photo-upload tool Templated pricing engine capturing the owner’s pricing logic Auto-generated, branded quote PDF sent within minutes Automated 3-day / 7-day follow-up nudges on unanswered quotes Instant e-sign / deposit collection built into the quote Guarantee An “anti-guarantee”: if close rate doesn’t improve in 30 days, the business is paid a penalty — signaling extreme confidence. Bonus A speed-to-lead comparison report showing industry conversion-decay data next to their own current average response time. Offer 3 — “The Silent Revenue System” (Post-Service Follow-Up) Dream Outcome Every completed job automatically turns into a 5-star review, a rebooked future job, or a referral — with no one needing to remember to ask. Core Promise “We’ll show you the exact dollar value sitting in your dormant customer list in 48 hours — for free, no commitment — then guarantee we recover at least [X%] of it in 60 days or we keep working until we do.” The Stack Job-completion trigger that auto-fires a pre-filtered review request Recurring-service tracker that flags customers due for their next visit Automated referral ask sent 2-3 days after service, at peak satisfaction Dashboard showing $ value of dormant customers who haven’t rebooked Guarantee 20 new reviews or $[X] in identified rebooking revenue in 60 days, or the client doesn’t pay. Bonus A free dormant-customer list pulled from existing records in week one — tangible, pre-payment proof of money on the table. The Bundled Grand Slam Name: “The Full-Booking Machine” (or “Zero-Leak System”) “We plug the three biggest leaks costing service businesses six figures a year — missed calls, slow quotes, and forgotten follow-up — and guarantee measurable results in 30-60 days.” Cascading guarantee: if scheduling doesn’t hit its number, quoting is free. If quoting doesn’t hit its number, follow-up is free too. If none of it works, the client pays nothing and keeps everything built. This makes the bundle feel nearly risk-free while remaining strong precisely because each component guarantee is independently strong. The Money Model Goal: recover customer acquisition cost within 30 days (ideally 24-48 hours), then compound revenue through continuity and upsells. Structured as a sequence of asks, not one static price. 1. Attraction Offer — Get to “Yes” Fast A paid (not free) diagnostic — R97-R997 — filters real buyers from tire-kickers and covers acquisition cost. Converts cold traffic into a paying customer on day one; everything after this is an upsell to an existing customer. 2. Core Offer — Front-Load the Setup Revenue Setup/implementation fee, paid upfront in one transaction — not spread across a payment plan. Justified directly by the diagnostic’s own numbers, not by comparison to competitor pricing. 3. Continuity Offer — Recurring Revenue Stacked On Top Monthly management/optimization fee, framed as ongoing tuning and monitoring — never as a “software fee.” This is where lifetime value compounds after the setup fee has already returned the acquisition cost. 4. Downsell / Upsell Ladder Downsell: if the full bundle is declined, offer a single system at a lower price point with the same upfront structure. Upsell: once one system is proven (about 30 days in), pitch the next system using the client’s own results as proof. Sequencing Timeline Day 0 — Paid diagnostic (R97-R500): cash in immediately, near-zero friction. Day 1-3 — Pitch the core offer using their own diagnostic numbers; close on a large upfront setup fee. Day 3-30 — Deliver a fast, visible win to justify the spend and set up the next upsell. Day 30+ — Layer in monthly continuity. Day 45-60 — Upsell system #2 and #3 using proven results from system #1. Caveat: front-loading cash only works long-term if delivery keeps pace with the money. If the early quick win doesn’t materialize, this model produces refund requests and reputation damage — which is more expensive than slower revenue. The upfront-cash structure should reflect genuinely fast delivery, not just a collection tactic. Price Points Ranges will flex by niche (HVAC vs. med spa vs. law firm), but this is a solid starting anchor. Higher end for businesses with higher average job values (contractors, dental, legal); lower end for lower-ticket services (cleaning, salons). Positioning rule of thumb: price the setup fee relative to the pain number surfaced in the diagnostic, not against “what similar software costs.” If the diagnostic showed R4,000/month in missed-call leakage, an R8,000 one-time setup fee is an easy yes on a two-month payback. Diagnostic → Core Offer Sales Sequence (Day 0-3) Day 0 — Diagnostic Delivery Call (15-20 min) Deliver findings live on a call, not just by email — the number lands harder spoken than read. Structure: what we found → what it’s costing monthly → specifically where it’s leaking. End with a single open question, not a pitch, to get verbal agreement the problem is real. The Transition Bridge directly from the agreed-upon number to permission for the pitch — a yes/no the prospect has already been primed to say yes to. The Pitch Show the specific system mapped directly to the leak identified. Anchor price against their own number (e.g., “less than X weeks of what you’re currently losing”). State the guarantee explicitly before it can be raised as an objection. If No Close on the Call — 72-Hour Follow-Up +24 hours — Recap email with the specific diagnostic numbers plus a short personalized video walkthrough. +48 hours — Case study / proof from a similar business facing the same leak. +72 hours — Scarcity/urgency close (genuine onboarding capacity limits only). Key principle: every touchpoint re-references the prospect’s own diagnostic numbers, never generic value props. The diagnostic is the entire argument for the rest of the sale. Offering | Structure | Typical Range Diagnostic (self-serve/light) | One-time, paid attraction offer | R97 - R297 Diagnostic (hands-on) | One-time, paid attraction offer | R500 - R997 Single-system setup | One-time core offer (1 of 3 systems) | R1,500 - R4,000 Full 3-system bundle setup | One-time core offer, bundled discount | R5,000 - R12,000 Single-system continuity | Monthly recurring | R200 - R500 / mo Full-bundle continuity | Monthly recurring | R750 - R2,000 / mo

Converts cold traffic into a paying customer on day one; everything after this is an upsell to an existing customer. 2. Core Offer — Front-Load the Setup Revenue Setup/implementation fee, paid upfront in one transaction — not spread across a payment plan. Justified directly by the diagnostic’s own numbers, not by comparison to competitor pricing. 3. Continuity Offer — Recurring Revenue Stacked On Top Monthly management/optimization fee, framed as ongoing tuning and monitoring — never as a “software fee.” This is where lifetime value compounds after the setup fee has already returned the acquisition cost. 4. Downsell / Upsell Ladder Downsell: if the full bundle is declined, offer a single system at a lower price point with the same upfront structure. Upsell: once one system is proven (about 30 days in), pitch the next system using the client’s own results as proof. Sequencing Timeline Day 0 — Paid diagnostic ($97-$500): cash in immediately, near-zero friction. Day 1-3 — Pitch the core offer using their own diagnostic numbers; close on a large upfront setup fee. Day 3-30 — Deliver a fast, visible win to justify the spend and set up the next upsell. Day 30+ — Layer in monthly continuity. Day 45-60 — Upsell system #2 and #3 using proven results from system #1. Caveat: front-loading cash only works long-term if delivery keeps pace with the money. If the early quick win doesn’t materialize, this model produces refund requests and reputation damage — which is more expensive than slower revenue. The upfront-cash structure should reflect genuinely fast delivery, not just a collection tactic. Price Points Ranges will flex by niche (HVAC vs. med spa vs. law firm), but this is a solid starting anchor. Higher end for businesses with higher average job values (contractors, dental, legal); lower end for lower-ticket services (cleaning, salons). Positioning rule of thumb: price the setup fee relative to the pain number surfaced in the diagnostic, not against “what similar software costs.” If the diagnostic showed $4,000/month in missed-call leakage, an $8,000 one-time setup fee is an easy yes on a two-month payback. Diagnostic → Core Offer Sales Sequence (Day 0-3) Day 0 — Diagnostic Delivery Call (15-20 min) Deliver findings live on a call, not just by email — the number lands harder spoken than read. Structure: what we found → what it’s costing monthly → specifically where it’s leaking. End with a single open question, not a pitch, to get verbal agreement the problem is real. The Transition Bridge directly from the agreed-upon number to permission for the pitch — a yes/no the prospect has already been primed to say yes to. The Pitch Show the specific system mapped directly to the leak identified. Anchor price against their own number (e.g., “less than X weeks of what you’re currently losing”). State the guarantee explicitly before it can be raised as an objection. If No Close on the Call — 72-Hour Follow-Up +24 hours — Recap email with the specific diagnostic numbers plus a short personalized video walkthrough. +48 hours — Case study / proof from a similar business facing the same leak. +72 hours — Scarcity/urgency close (genuine onboarding capacity limits only). Key principle: every touchpoint re-references the prospect’s own diagnostic numbers, never generic value props. The diagnostic is the entire argument for the rest of the sale. The Diagnostic Call Script Opening (1 min) — Set the Frame “Thanks for jumping on, [Name]. This should take about 15 minutes. I pulled the numbers from [their call log / CRM / booking data] and built out exactly where you’re leaking revenue right now. I’ll walk you through what I found, and then it’s up to you what you want to do with it — no pitch, just the numbers first. Sound good?” Explicitly saying “no pitch” lowers their guard and makes the number land more credibly. Deliver the Finding (5-7 min) “So here’s the headline: based on [X missed calls last month / average quote turnaround of Y days / Z dormant customers], you’re leaving roughly $[amount] a month on the table. Let me show you where that’s coming from.” Walk through 2-3 specific, dated examples from their own data — not hypotheticals: “For example, on [specific date], a call came in at 2:14pm and it went to voicemail — no callback, no text, nothing. That customer likely called your competitor. We saw this pattern [X] times last month.” The Pause — Get Verbal Agreement “Does that number surprise you, or does that roughly track with what you expected?” Let them answer, then reflect it back: “Yeah, that’s really common — most [industry] businesses we look at are losing somewhere in that range, and almost none of them know it until they see it laid out like this.” The Bridge to the Offer “So knowing that number — would it be useful if I showed you exactly what we’d build to close that gap?” The Offer (3-5 min) “Here’s what we’d set up: [plain-English description]. It’s a one-time build fee of $[X] — which, based on what we just looked at, pays for itself in about [X weeks]. And to be clear on risk: [guarantee]. If we don’t hit [specific number] in [timeframe], [guarantee terms].” Close “Does it make sense to move forward, or do you have questions first?” Silence after this. Let them respond — don’t fill the pause. 72-Hour Follow-Up Email Sequence +24 Hours — Recap + Personalized Proof Subject: Your [X]/monthleak—quickrecapHey[Name], quickrecapfromourcall—here′swhatwefound : [specificstat1]; [specificstat2]; totalimpact: [X]/month. I put together a 90-second walkthrough of exactly what we’d build for [Business Name] specifically: [video link]. No rush — just wanted the numbers in front of you in writing. Happy to answer anything. [Name] +48 Hours — Proof / Case Study Subject: How [similar business] fixed the same leak Hey [Name], thought this might be useful — [Similar Business Type] had almost the exact same issue we found in your numbers ([specific similar stat]). After we set up [system name], they [specific result — e.g. “cut no-shows by 43% in the first month”]. Happy to jump back on a quick call if you want to talk through how this would apply to [Business Name] — otherwise just let me know if you’ve got questions. [Name] +72 Hours — Scarcity / Urgency Close Subject: Last thing on this Hey [Name], didn’t want to keep bugging you, so this is the last note on this — we can only onboard a few new builds this month to make sure delivery stays fast for everyone (this is a hands-on setup, not a self-serve tool). If it’s a “yes, just not right now,” totally fine — the numbers we found aren’t going anywhere and I’m happy to reconnect whenever’s better. If you want to lock in this month, here’s a link to grab a time: [booking link]. Either way, appreciate you letting me dig into your numbers. [Name] Caution: only use the scarcity line if the onboarding cap is real. Fabricated scarcity is the fastest way to lose trust with relationship-driven, referral-heavy customers in small, connected local markets — where it tends to surface. Merged AI Automation Full Booking Machine

AI AUTOMATION SERVICES Pricing & Service Packages Helping businesses automate repetitive work, respond faster, capture more leads and improve customer service. Featuring The Full-Booking Machine — A Grand Slam Offer System for Service-Based SMBs How Our Pricing Works Each project can be purchased as a once-off implementation or as a monthly managed service. The once-off fee covers the design, setup, configuration, integrations, testing and launch of the automation. The monthly fee covers ongoing hosting/automation management, monitoring, maintenance, support, AI/API usage allowances and optimisation. The Problems We Solve Service-based SMBs (contractors, agencies, salons, med/dental, consultants, repair shops) lose revenue to three operational leaks. Each leak is automatable, and each has been packaged into a named, guaranteed offer using the Grand Slam Offer framework: maximise dream outcome and perceived likelihood of success, minimise time delay and effort, then wrap in guarantees, bonuses and scarcity. The Three Core Problems Scheduling, Dispatch & No-Shows — phone-tag, double-booking, no reminders, high-friction rescheduling. Quoting & Estimate Generation — slow manual quotes, pricing trapped in one person’s head, no follow-up after the quote is sent. Post-Service Follow-Up — no owner of the review/rebooking/referral step, no systematic timing, awkward in-person asks. Package Overview 1. BASIC PACKAGE Once-off setup: R1,500 | Monthly management: R499/month A simple entry-level automation designed for small businesses that want to remove one repetitive task and improve how they handle customer enquiries or leads. What We Will Do We identify one repetitive process in the business that can be automated. We design one automation workflow around that process. We connect the required platform, such as WhatsApp, email, Google Forms or Google Sheets. We configure the automated responses, actions and basic business rules. We test the workflow from start to finish and launch it. We provide basic post-launch support to make sure the system works as intended. What’s Included 1 automation workflow Basic AI chatbot or automated response system Lead capture WhatsApp OR email automation Google Sheets/database connection Basic workflow configuration Testing and launch 7 days post-launch support Basic monthly monitoring and maintenance on the managed plan Example Use Case A salon receives enquiries on WhatsApp. The system can automatically answer common questions, collect the customer’s name and service request, and save the lead for the business. 2. STANDARD PACKAGE Once-off setup: R3,500 | Monthly management: R999/month A multi-automation package for businesses that want to automate several customer and lead-management processes. What We Will Do We review the client’s current customer journey and identify multiple repetitive tasks. We build up to three connected automation workflows. We connect customer enquiries to a lead-capture system or spreadsheet. We configure automatic follow-ups and reminders. We connect booking or appointment processes where required. We test all workflows together and launch the system. What’s Included Up to 3 automation workflows AI-powered chatbot WhatsApp automation Lead capture and management Automatic follow-up messages Email automation Google Forms/Sheets integration Basic appointment/booking automation Basic reporting Monthly maintenance Priority support on the managed plan Example Use Case A barber shop can use the system to answer FAQs, collect customer details, send booking information, confirm appointments and automatically follow up with customers who enquire but do not book. 3. PROFESSIONAL PACKAGE Once-off setup: R7,500 | Monthly management: R1,999/month A more advanced automation system for businesses that want AI to manage a significant part of their lead, customer-service and booking workflow. What We Will Do We map the client’s existing workflow and identify opportunities for automation. We build up to seven automation workflows that work together. We configure an AI assistant around the client’s services, FAQs, policies and business information. We connect lead qualification, follow-ups, bookings and customer communication. We integrate the system with a CRM or suitable customer database where required. We create reporting so the business can track leads and automation activity. We test, launch and optimise the system. What’s Included Up to 7 automation workflows Advanced AI chatbot/assistant WhatsApp lead qualification Automated customer follow-ups Booking system integration CRM integration Email + WhatsApp workflows AI-generated customer responses Lead scoring Automated reminders Dashboard/reporting Monthly optimisation Priority support Monitoring and maintenance on the managed plan Example Use Case A car dealership can have an AI assistant answer vehicle questions, collect a buyer’s requirements, qualify the lead, record the lead in a CRM, send follow-ups and notify a salesperson when a high-quality lead is ready. 4. We configure monitoring and error handling so problems can be identified quickly. We test the complete system, launch it and continuously optimise it under the managed plan. What’s Included Custom AI automation system Unlimited* automation workflows Advanced WhatsApp automation AI sales/customer-service agent Lead qualification and scoring Automated sales follow-ups CRM integration Booking and appointment automation Email/SMS/WhatsApp workflows AI document processing AI-generated reports Custom dashboard Business-specific AI knowledge base Analytics and performance tracking Monitoring and maintenance Continuous optimisation Priority support Example Use Case A growing company can have one connected system that captures enquiries, qualifies leads, answers customer questions, books appointments, updates the CRM, sends follow-ups, generates reports and alerts staff when human intervention is needed. The Full-Booking Machine — Signature Offer System Each of the three core problems above has a root cause breakdown and a named, guaranteed Grand Slam Offer built around fixing it. These offers can be sold individually or bundled, and map directly onto the packages above depending on scope and workflow count. Root Cause Breakdown: Scheduling, Dispatch & No-Shows Core sub-problems Phone-tag bottleneck — short-staffed businesses miss calls; missed calls become the next competitor’s lead. Double-booking / capacity blindness — manual calendars (or paper) cause overlaps and gaps. No buffer/travel-time logic — field jobs booked without drive time, causing cascading lateness. Forgetting = no-show — customers book and simply forget, especially for dates more than a few days out. Rescheduling friction — moving an appointment requires a call, so customers no-show instead. What automation fixes AI phone/chat answering removes the phone-tag bottleneck. Smart calendar tooling removes double-booking and adds buffer logic. Multi-touch automated reminders (48hr / 24hr / 2hr) cut no-shows. Self-service reschedule links remove the friction behind silent no-shows. Root Cause Breakdown: Quoting & Estimate Generation Core sub-problems Estimation requires manual site visits/measurement, adding days of delay. Pricing logic lives in the owner’s head — a single point of failure for quoting. Quote formatting/assembly is a manual 20-30 minute task that gets deprioritized. No urgency after the quote is sent — warm leads go cold waiting. Inconsistent pricing across similar jobs erodes trust and margin. What automation fixes Photo-based AI estimating or structured intake forms remove the need for an in-person visit. Templated pricing rules capture the owner’s knowledge into a repeatable system. Auto-generated, branded quote documents remove assembly time. Automated follow-up sequences keep quoted leads warm without manual chasing. Root Cause Breakdown: Post-Service Follow-Up Core sub-problems Nobody owns the follow-up step once a job is marked done. Timing is manual and inconsistent — asks happen sporadically, not systematically. No visibility into rebooking windows for recurring-service customers. Asking for referrals in person feels awkward, so it rarely happens. Review requests aren’t filtered, risking public complaints from unhappy customers. What automation fixes Job-completion triggers auto-fire a follow-up sequence with zero reliance on staff memory. Timed drip campaigns solve the rebooking blind spot for recurring services. Automated, well-timed referral asks remove the awkward in-person moment. Pre-filtered review requests protect the public rating while still capturing feedback. Offer 1 — “The Never-Miss System” (Scheduling / No-Shows) Dream Outcome Fill every open slot on the calendar and never lose a job to a missed call or a no-show again. Core Promise “We’ll recover $[X] in lost bookings in your first 14 days — using your own missed-call log as the baseline — or we run it free until we do, and you keep everything we built.” The Stack AI phone/chat answering that books jobs 24/7, even after hours Smart calendar with auto-buffer/travel-time logic 3-touch automated reminder sequence (48hr / 24hr / 2hr) One-click self-serve reschedule Missed-call text-back so no lead calls a competitor Guarantee Performance-based, tied to a measurable number recovered within 14 days — not a vague activity promise. Bonus A done-for-you missed-call recovery in week one — a fast, visible win using real texted-back leads before asking for any long-term commitment. Offer 2 — “Quote-to-Close in 24 Hours” (Quoting) Dream Outcome Turn every inquiry into a professional quote same-day, without lifting a finger — and win more jobs by being first to respond. Core Promise “Every inquiry gets a professional quote in under an hour, automatically — and if your close rate doesn’t go up within 30 days, we don’t just refund you, we pay you $[X] for wasting your time.” The Stack Structured intake form / photo-upload tool Templated pricing engine capturing the owner’s pricing logic Auto-generated, branded quote PDF sent within minutes Automated 3-day / 7-day follow-up nudges on unanswered quotes Instant e-sign / deposit collection built into the quote Guarantee An “anti-guarantee”: if close rate doesn’t improve in 30 days, the business is paid a penalty — signaling extreme confidence. Bonus A speed-to-lead comparison report showing industry conversion-decay data next to their own current average response time. Offer 3 — “The Silent Revenue System” (Post-Service Follow-Up) Dream Outcome Every completed job automatically turns into a 5-star review, a rebooked future job, or a referral — with no one needing to remember to ask. Core Promise “We’ll show you the exact dollar value sitting in your dormant customer list in 48 hours — for free, no commitment — then guarantee we recover at least [X%] of it in 60 days or we keep working until we do.” The Stack Job-completion trigger that auto-fires a pre-filtered review request Recurring-service tracker that flags customers due for their next visit Automated referral ask sent 2-3 days after service, at peak satisfaction Dashboard showing $ value of dormant customers who haven’t rebooked Guarantee 20 new reviews or $[X] in identified rebooking revenue in 60 days, or the client doesn’t pay. Bonus A free dormant-customer list pulled from existing records in week one — tangible, pre-payment proof of money on the table. Offer stack strategy

The offer stack A job application built like a Grand Slam Offer — tool, resume, cover letter, video 1. Build priority Build in this order — sequencing beats parallelizing. Each asset should be sharp enough to not be a bottleneck for the next one before you move on. A stacked offer at 80% sent this week beats a perfect one sent in six weeks to a role that’s already filled. 2. CLOSER applied to the application video CLOSER was built for sales conversations — and a job application video is a sales conversation. You’re selling a decision (hire me), not a product. C — Clarify why you’re there: Name the exact reason you’re sending this. No fluff intro. L — Label the problem: Show you understand the actual gap they’re hiring to fill, not the job description. O — Overview the pain: What does it cost them to keep hiring around this gap? Slower ramp, lost deals, wasted training. S — Sell the outcome, not the plane ride: Don’t talk about your resume. Talk about what their team looks like 90 days after they hire you. E — Explain away objections: Preempt the “not enough experience” objection on camera, before they think it. R — Reinforce the decision: Close with certainty — not “hope to hear from you,” but a clear next step. 3. Ten things “above and beyond” looks like Solve a real problem the company has, before they hire you. Reference something specific — an earnings call, launch, or post — not generic flattery. Send a video, not just a PDF. Voice and face are underused leverage. Include a first-30-days plan specific to their team. Get a warm intro or reference from someone who’s worked with them or a competitor. Show the work — link the code, the deck, the demo, don’t just claim it. Follow up with new value each time, never just “checking in.” Point out and constructively solve a problem in their public product or content. Quantify impact everywhere — numbers beat adjectives. Make their job easy — one clean link with everything organized. 4. Making yourself the undeniable candidate The real constraint in hiring is risk — will this person perform, or are they another expensive mistake? Every unproven candidate is a bet. Your job is to remove the bet, not just ask for it to be taken. Proof of skill — the tool you built Proof of initiative — you built it unprompted, for them specifically Proof of fit — you speak their language and know their pain Proof of low risk — you show exactly how you’d ramp, so there’s no guessing You’re not asking to be picked. You’re presenting evidence and letting them judge. That reframes the entire power dynamic. 5. Leverage: does it matter here? Yes — companies just call it “signal.” A resume is a claim. A working product is proof. Most applicants are all claim, no proof — that’s the gap you exploit. Does the sales-call transcription tool provide immense value? Run it through the value equation: Value = (Dream outcome × Perceived likelihood) ÷ (Time delay × Effort) If the tool surfaces real patterns — objection-handling gaps, close-rate killers, talk-time ratios that predict lost deals — that’s a dream outcome (more revenue), delivered with near-zero effort on their part and no time delay, since you can show results now instead of asking them to trust you later. That’s immense value. If it’s just “a script that transcribes calls,” that’s a commodity — Otter.ai already does that for free. The value isn’t the transcription. It’s the pattern-recognition and business impact. Lead your pitch with that, not the tech stack. Other leverage to bring Any dataset or research specific to their industry A cold outreach campaign you ran that got real replies Case studies from past roles with numbers attached Content (posts, videos) that shows you understand their market Referrals or introductions from people they respect A mockup or audit of their current process, showing exactly where it breaks Speed — respond and deliver faster than anyone else in the pipeline Specificity — generic candidates get generic outcomes, hyper-specific ones get remembered 6. Stacking it all — and the odds Stacked, these assets compound instead of adding — you remove every excuse to say no while giving multiple reasons to say yes. Most candidates give one weak signal (a resume). You’re giving four reinforcing signals that all point the same direction: this person already thinks and operates like someone who works here. Realistically: this doesn’t guarantee an offer, but it moves you from “one of 200 resumes” to “the person we’re talking about internally” — from being evaluated to being sought. That shift is the actual win, and it’s what compounds into offers over multiple applications. 7. What to ask for instead of money Skills compound; a slightly higher starting salary doesn’t. Frame the ask as a trade, not a favor: “I bring speed and initiative — in exchange I want reps and access most people at my level don’t get.” Access — sit in on strategy calls, leadership meetings, deals above your pay grade Mentorship — direct time with the best performer or the founder, not just your manager Scope — ownership of a project outside your “lane” to prove range Speed of feedback — faster review cycles to compound learning quicker Cross-training — time in adjacent departments even if your role is fixed Public reps — presenting, pitching, or client-facing work early, even if uncomfortable Go build the offer stack and make it embarrassing for them to hire anyone else. 1. The tool One sharp, provable insight — not a polished product | 2. Resume Tight, quantified, zero friction | 3. Cover letter Bridges the tool to their specific gap | 4. Video CLOSER-structured, references the other three

Offers and specs

Value ladder pricing model

CONVERSION COPYWRITER VALUE LADDER & PRICING MODEL Built on Hormozi’s value equation, grand slam offer framework, and wealth ladder principles 6 tiers. From free to $10,000/month. Every tier earns trust, solves one problem, and reveals the next. THE HORMOZI FRAMEWORK APPLIED Hormozi’s core insight: the business that provides the most value wins. But value is not what you think you provide — it is what the buyer believes they receive, relative to what they pay and what they risk. His value equation: Value = (Dream Outcome × Perceived Likelihood of Achievement) ÷ (Time Delay × Effort & Sacrifice). To charge more, you do not add more features. You increase the dream outcome, increase the perceived certainty it will work, reduce how long it takes, and reduce how hard it is for the client. Applied to a conversion copywriting practice, this means every tier of the value ladder must answer the same four questions — just at progressively higher stakes, higher certainty, and higher price: The Wealth Ladder principle — why the model is built top-down Hormozi’s wealth ladder shows that the best businesses get paid before they work, repeatedly, without the payment stopping when the work stops. Most freelancers are at the bottom: they work, then invoice. The goal of this model is to ascend you toward the top — recurring revenue paid upfront, compounding over time. The model is built from the top down in this document for two reasons. First, so you understand what you are building toward. Second, so every decision about lower tiers — pricing, positioning, what to include — is made in service of ascension to the top, not as standalone products. The Grand Slam Offer at every tier Hormozi’s Grand Slam Offer principle: every offer must be so good that the buyer feels stupid saying no. The way to achieve this is not to lower the price — it is to make the value so clear, and the perceived risk so low, that the price feels like a fraction of what they are getting. The tool he uses: value stacking — listing every component of the offer separately and pricing each one, then revealing the total package price. THE 6-TIER VALUE LADDER Six tiers. Each one solves a complete problem. Each one creates the natural desire for the next. This is the full architecture of the model. Tiers 1 and 2 build trust and reveal the problem. Tiers 3 and 4 are the core revenue engine. Tier 5 is the retainer goal. Tier 6 is the highest-value offer — for a small number of clients who want the full system. EACH TIER IN FULL TIER 1 The lead magnet does one job: turn a stranger into a warm prospect by giving them a number they cannot unsee. Hormozi’s rule — give away the what and the why, sell the how. The lead magnet shows them what the problem is and why it exists. The diagnosis call shows them specifically how to fix their version of it. TIER 2 This is the Hormozi ‘free strategy call’ model applied correctly. The call is genuinely useful — not a thinly veiled sales pitch. The founder leaves with a specific, actionable written list regardless of what they buy. Because the call is useful, the conversion rate to Tier 3 is high — typically 40–60% of diagnosis calls convert to a paid audit. Why free — and how it converts Hormozi on free offers: the best businesses give away things their competitors charge for. When you give a founder a 30-minute specific teardown that would cost $300 at an agency, you create three things simultaneously: demonstrated expertise, established trust, and the natural desire for the deeper fix. The audit ($500) feels cheap relative to what they just received for free. TIER 3 The $500 price point — why this number Hormozi’s principle: the entry-point price must be low enough that it feels like a ‘stupid not to’ decision, but high enough that it filters for serious buyers. At $500, a founder who does the revenue gap calculation — and sees that their copy gap is costing them $100,000+ per year — is not asking whether $500 is worth it. They are asking when can we start. The $500 also does something critical: it removes the ‘something for nothing’ anxiety. Founders who pay for the audit are invested. They read it thoroughly. They implement the recommendations. They become better case studies. And their commitment to the process makes the Tier 4 project conversation natural rather than a hard sell. TIER 4 Pricing this project correctly — the Hormozi anchoring method Most copywriters price the homepage project based on their hourly rate. Hormozi prices based on the value delivered. The anchor is the revenue gap number from the calculator. Use it every time: Price range rationale — $4,500 to $7,500 TIER 5 — THE GOAL STATE The retainer conversation — when and how Hormozi’s principle: do not pitch the next tier. Reveal the next problem. At the handover of every completed project, the conversation is: Retainer MRR targets — the compounding model Three retainers at $4,000 per month is the target state: $144,000 annual recurring revenue as the income floor, with project work adding on top. At this point, the business development effort required is approximately 20% of what it takes to continuously hunt for new project clients. This is the compounding advantage Hormozi describes — you have climbed the wealth ladder to the point where your income does not stop when your outreach stops. TIER 6 — THE GRAND SLAM OFFER Who this is for and how to sell it Tier 6 is for a specific type of founder: post-Series A, $3M–$15M ARR, running paid acquisition, and ready to treat copy as a strategic function rather than a project. The tell-tale sign: they are spending $30,000–$100,000 per month on paid ads and have never overhauled the copy those ads point to. One Tier 6 project at $20,000 is 2–4 weeks of their ad spend — and it improves the ROI of every subsequent month’s spend permanently. Value stack for the Tier 6 offer THE ASCENSION MODEL — HOW CLIENTS MOVE UP The value ladder only works if every tier naturally creates the desire for the next one. This section shows you exactly how each transition works — what you say, when you say it, and what makes saying yes feel obvious. Tier 1 → 2: Lead magnet to diagnosis call The lead magnet reveals the problem. The diagnosis call solves the diagnostic problem. The transition happens when the founder finishes the calculator and sees their gap number. At that moment, the next question in their head is: ‘But what specifically is causing this in my copy?’ The diagnosis call answers that question. Tier 2 → 3: Diagnosis call to messaging audit The diagnosis call surfaces 3–5 specific problems in their copy. The written priority list delivered after the call contains the observations — but not the full solutions. The audit contains the full solutions, with evidence. The transition happens when the founder reads the priority list and realises each item could be fixed, but they do not have the time or expertise to know how to implement each change correctly without making it worse. Tier 3 → 4: Messaging audit to homepage project The audit tells the founder exactly what is wrong. Reading it creates a new problem: they now know what needs to change but recognise that implementing it — while running a company — is not how they want to spend their next three weeks. The project solves that problem. Tier 4 → 5: Project to retainer The project produces results — a measurable before/after conversion improvement. The retainer maintains and compounds those results. The transition happens at the project handover when the founder sees the before/after data and realises that the homepage is fixed but the onboarding sequence, the outbound copy, and the paid ad creative are still running on the old copy. Tier 5 → 6: Retainer to conversion system Tier 6 is for the subset of Tier 5 clients who want to compress time. After 3–4 months of retainer work, the founder has seen consistent results. Some will want to do the full-funnel build in a concentrated 90-day sprint — especially if they are about to raise a round, launch a product, or scale paid acquisition significantly. The transition is opportunity-triggered, not time-triggered. THE REVENUE MODEL — MONTH BY MONTH What this model produces in revenue at each stage of build. Built on realistic conversion rates, not best-case assumptions. Months 1–3: Build the engine Months 4–6: Compound the base Months 7–12: The retainer floor THE GUARANTEE — HORMOZI’S RISK REVERSAL Hormozi’s principle: the person who takes all the risk, wins all the clients. Remove the risk from the buyer and you remove the biggest block to saying yes. The anxiety that kills the most deals in your niche: ‘What if I spend $5,500 and the copy doesn’t convert any better?’ That fear is legitimate. The founder has been burned before. The guarantee is your answer to that fear — made concrete, specific, and credible. The guarantee at each tier THE ONE-PAGE SUMMARY The complete model on one page. Pin this up. You do not need 100 clients. You need 3 retainers and a pipeline of projects. Build the top of the ladder first. Every other decision flows from it. Charge what it is worth. Guarantee the outcome. Remove the risk. Ascend. Hormozi’s guarantee rule: The guarantee should make you nervous to offer — because if you are not nervous, it is not strong enough to move the buyer. A good guarantee only works if you are confident enough in your delivery to stand behind it. If you skip the research phase, you cannot offer this guarantee.
